paragraphs: Here's what this whole chapter comes down to, friend: where are your roots? The LORD says, "Cursed is the man who trusts in mankind, who makes mere flesh his strength and turns his heart from the LORD." (Jeremiah 17:5) Then He says, "But blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in Him." (Jeremiah 17:7) Two roads, two ends, and the LORD wants you to see both before you pick.

Now watch what the tree does. It is "planted by the waters" and "sends out its roots toward the stream," so when the heat comes, it does not fear, and in a year of drought it does not cease to produce fruit. (Jeremiah 17:8) That tree never promised the heat would stay away. It just had somewhere to drink while it was hot. And I know my own heart, friend, since the LORD says it is "deceitful above all things" (Jeremiah 17:9), which is why I don't let it drive when I'm hungry and the cookies are cooling.

The good news is that the LORD doesn't leave us guessing, because He says, "I, the LORD, search the heart." (Jeremiah 17:10) The prayer at the end calls Him "the fountain of living water" (Jeremiah 17:13) and says, "Heal me, O LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for You are my praise." (Jeremiah 17:14) So when the heat comes, and it will, run to the stream. Stay rooted in Him, and you'll still be bearing fruit when everybody else is crunchy.
